AMGN.rationale: Amgen presents a mildly attractive fundamental case. The business is growing revenue mid-single digits (+5.8% YoY in Q1 2026) with meaningful margin expansion (gross margin 68.1%, operating margin 30.9%, net margin 21% vs 13% prior year) and strong cash flow improvement (OCF +57.4% YoY). Valuation has compressed to the low end of its 12-month P/E range (24.7x vs 22.6–49.7x range), partly driven by the earnings improvement itself. The franchise is genuinely diversified with multiple growth engines (Repatha +34% YoY, TEPEZZA +29% YoY) and management raised 2026 guidance to $37.1B–$38.5B revenue. However, the case is capped at mildly attractive due to: (1) extreme balance-sheet leverage at 6.24x D/E ($57.32B debt on $9.19B equity) leaving no margin of safety; (2) the denosumab patent cliff is actively accelerating (Prolia -33.85% in Q1 2026) creating a timing gap with growth assets; (3) the margin improvement cannot be fully verified through a complete TTM due to fiscal reporting gaps; (4) earnings yield of 4.0% sits below the 10Y Treasury at 4.45%, thinning the equity risk premium. The advisory note that non-GAAP EPS of $5.15 implies a materially lower P/E (~17.3x) is noted but the GAAP-based 24.7x is the raw data metric. MariTide obesity pipeline optionality is real but Phase 3 readouts are not yet available, making it a future catalyst rather than a current one. The Tavneos FDA withdrawal proposal adds contained but real regulatory risk. Overall: solid franchise in a contested transition, fairly valued given the risks, with the next full quarterly results needed to confirm margin durability.
